screening_decisions.reason: This is an RCT (82 patients randomized) with adults (mean age 75 years) with HF comparing a tablet computer with specialized software containing HF information and lifestyle advice versus standard HF information only. The tablet-based education meets the mHealth education criteria.

This is an RCT (450 patients in three-group parallel-randomized trial) with stable HF patients (mean age 66.8 years) comparing the heartfailurematters.org website on top of usual care versus usual care. The website-based education meets the mHealth education criteria.

This is an RCT (28 participants in randomized controlled design) with HF patients comparing a web-based self-care intervention versus control. The web-based education meets the mHealth education criteria.

This is an RCT (75 patients randomized to three groups) with HF patients comparing SMS follow-up versus telephone and regular follow-up. SMS messages meet the mHealth education criteria as specified in the protocol.

This is an RCT with HF patients, but the intervention is primarily nurse-led face-to-face counseling with computer-based education as an adjunct, not mHealth-delivered education via smartphones/tablets/apps/SMS/social media.
This is an RCT with HF patients, but the intervention is nurse-led counseling with computer-based education and written materials, not mHealth-delivered education via mobile devices.

This is an RCT with HF patients, but the intervention is nurse-guided education program with facilitated telephone communication and follow-up visits, not mHealth-delivered education via mobile devices.

This is an RCT with HF patients, but the intervention is video education (VE) in addition to standard education. Video education is not mHealth-delivered education as it is not delivered via smartphones/tablets/apps/SMS/social media.

This is a pilot usability study with 8 patients, not an RCT. The study aimed to understand challenges and provide design considerations for an mHealth system, not to compare mHealth education versus usual care.
This is an analysis of the recruitment process for an mHealth study, not an RCT evaluating mHealth education versus usual care. The paper reports on recruitment challenges and refusal rates.

This is an RCT (18 patients randomized) with HF patients comparing a web-based compliance monitoring device versus usual care. While primarily monitoring, the web-based system may include educational components. Being conservative, I include this study.
This is a proof of concept paper using exploratory inquiry with field study strategy, not an RCT. It does not compare mHealth education versus usual care.
This is a descriptive survey design assessing usability of a mobile app, not an RCT. It does not compare mHealth education versus usual care.
This is a study protocol paper, not results from a completed RCT. Additionally, the intervention includes home telemonitoring which is primarily monitoring rather than mHealth education.

This is an RCT with HF patients, but the intervention includes home telemonitoring and patient self-management support as part of a collaborative care model. Telemonitoring is primarily device-based monitoring, not mHealth education delivered via smartphones/tablets/apps/SMS/social media.
This is a study design paper, not results from a completed RCT. The intervention is primarily phone-based collaborative care with nurse and social worker, not mHealth education.
This is an RCT (six-month randomized field experiment) comparing a web-based HeartCareII resource versus usual care. The website-based education meets the mHealth education criteria.

This RCT uses telephone-based motivational interviewing, not mHealth-delivered education. The intervention is phone calls with motivational interviewing techniques, which does not meet the mHealth criteria (internet/web-based programs, apps, SMS, or social media for education delivery).

This study focuses on cardiovascular disease (CVD) population, not specifically heart failure patients. The design is described as an 'intervention trial' but not explicitly an RCT. The tablet application was used during in-person education sessions, not as standalone mHealth education delivery.

This is an RCT with HF patients comparing a mobile phone-assisted case management program vs usual care. The intervention evaluated self-care efficacy, knowledge, and behavior, suggesting educational components delivered via mobile phone technology. Meets mHealth education criteria.

This RCT uses telehomecare focused on monitoring clinical indices and detecting changes in cardiac status. The intervention is monitoring-based, not education delivery. Does not meet the mHealth-delivered education criteria.

This study uses telehealth systems for monitoring and communication, not for delivering education. The focus is on patient confidence and self-management through monitoring technology, not educational content delivery via mHealth.

This RCT uses the Health Buddy telehealth system for monitoring clinical status after discharge. While it may encourage self-care behaviors, the intervention is primarily monitoring-based rather than education delivery via mHealth.

This RCT uses internet-based synchronized face-to-face video sessions for education about exercise and self-care in HF patients. The intervention includes online group discussion/education sessions delivered via Vidyo software, meeting the mHealth-delivered education criteria.

This study uses a quasi-experimental design, not an RCT. Additionally, the computer assisted learning (CAL) program appears to be delivered on stationary computers in hospital, not via mobile devices (mHealth).
This is a development and feasibility study, not an RCT. It describes the process of developing a web-based program but does not test its effectiveness in a randomized trial.
This RCT delivers e-mail reminders to NURSES, not education to patients via mHealth. The intervention targets healthcare providers, not patients, and is not mHealth-delivered education.
This is a feasibility study using a convenience sample, not an RCT. While it uses an mHealth app with education components, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a study protocol/design paper for a telerehabilitation trial, not an education intervention. The focus is on cardiac rehabilitation with telemonitoring and telecoaching, not mHealth-delivered education.
This is a systematic literature review, not a primary RCT. Does not meet the study design criteria.
This RCT focuses on telemonitoring medication adherence, not delivering education. The intervention is about monitoring adherence behavior, not educational content delivery via mHealth.
This RCT includes patients with HF OR COPD (mixed population). The intervention is telehealth care delivery, not mHealth-delivered education. Focus is on integrated care, not education.
This RCT tests medication reminder systems (electronic pill box and smartphone app), not education delivery. The intervention is about reminders to take medications, not educational content.
This RCT uses the MedSentry remote medication monitoring system, which monitors adherence but does not deliver educational content. The intervention is monitoring-based, not education delivery.
Not a pure RCT (combines RCT and pragmatic designs); targets multiple conditions (COPD, cardiac failure, diabetes) not HF-specific; intervention is integrated care services not mHealth education
